why.detail: Someone with a calm schedule can still worry all day, and someone buried in tasks may not be worried at all, so people can tell which one they live with. Anxiety is worry about what might go wrong; Stress is having too much going on right now.

current.name: Anxiety
current.line: I worry too much.

proposed.name: Stress
proposed.line: I'm overwhelmed.

side.name: Stress
side.line: I'm overwhelmed.

side.name: Paperwork
side.line: I lose my week to forms, bills and phone queues.

why.detail: Paperwork is one specific cause with its own fixes, while being overwhelmed can come from work, family or anything else. Stress is the feeling of too much at once from any source; Paperwork is the time lost to forms, bills and phone queues.

current.name: Stress
current.line: I'm overwhelmed.

proposed.name: Paperwork
proposed.line: I lose my week to forms, bills and phone queues.

side.name: Anger
side.line: I snap at people I love.

side.name: Family
side.line: I'm caught in fighting at home.

why.detail: One is about how I react and the other is about the home I live in, and a person knows whether the problem is mostly them or the household. Short fuse is my own temper with people I love; Family is being caught in fighting at home that others start too.

current.name: Anger
current.line: I snap at people I love.

proposed.name: Family
proposed.line: I'm caught in fighting at home.

side.name: Anger
side.line: I snap at people I love.

side.name: Stress
side.line: I'm overwhelmed.

why.detail: Plenty of stressed people don't snap at anyone, and the fixes for a quick temper are different from the fixes for too much on my plate. Short fuse is how I treat people when I'm on edge; Stress is the load that may put me there.

current.name: Anger
current.line: I snap at people I love.

proposed.name: Stress
proposed.line: I'm overwhelmed.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Anxiety
side.line: I worry too much.

why.detail: They often come together, but people describe them very differently and would pick the one that sounds like their days. Feeling down is low mood and nothing seeming worth it; Anxiety is a mind racing with worry.

current.name: Depression
current.line: I feel low most days.

proposed.name: Anxiety
proposed.line: I worry too much.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Burnout
side.line: I've got nothing left.

why.detail: Burnout sits under Work because rest and changes at work help it, while feeling low most days reaches beyond work. Feeling down is low mood across life; Burnout is being worn out, usually by work.

current.name: Depression
current.line: I feel low most days.

proposed.name: Burnout
proposed.line: I've got nothing left.

side.name: Self-esteem
side.line: I'm never good enough for myself.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

why.detail: Many people who judge themselves harshly don't feel low most days, so they would choose without hesitating. Hard on myself is the voice that says I'm never good enough; Feeling down is a low mood that may have no such voice.

current.name: Self-esteem
current.line: I'm never good enough for myself.

proposed.name: Depression
proposed.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Trauma
side.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

why.detail: Someone shaped by a past event knows it is about that event, and it needs its own care and, later, its own crisis resources. Trauma is living with one thing that happened; Feeling down is a general low mood with or without a cause.

current.name: Trauma
current.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

proposed.name: Depression
proposed.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Trauma
side.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

side.name: Anxiety
side.line: I worry too much.

why.detail: The past event is the center of one and absent from the other, so the person living it can tell them apart. Trauma is about something that already happened; Anxiety is worry about what might happen.

current.name: Trauma
current.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

proposed.name: Anxiety
proposed.line: I worry too much.

side.name: Focus
side.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

side.name: Procrastination
side.line: I put things off.

why.detail: People know whether their trouble is getting going or staying with it, and the fixes differ. Can't focus is my attention drifting once I start; Procrastination is not starting at all.

current.name: Focus
current.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

proposed.name: Procrastination
proposed.line: I put things off.

side.name: Focus
side.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

side.name: Doomscrolling
side.line: I lose my nights to my phone.

why.detail: The phone is one cause of scattered attention, but plenty of people can't focus with the phone put away. Can't focus is attention that won't stay on any one thing; Doomscrolling is evenings lost to the phone.

current.name: Focus
current.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

proposed.name: Doomscrolling
proposed.line: I lose my nights to my phone.

side.name: Grief
side.line: I'm missing someone I lost.

side.name: Loneliness
side.line: I feel alone.

why.detail: A grieving person can be surrounded by family and still miss the one who died, so the two are easy to tell apart. Grief is missing one person I lost; Loneliness is not having people around me now.

current.name: Grief
current.line: I'm missing someone I lost.

proposed.name: Loneliness
proposed.line: I feel alone.
